Speaker: The Rescuer
Effective line: Behind me is the Forgotten Cave. Follow it all the way through to {town}. Someone there will be waiting for you.
Suggested line: Behind me is the Forgotten Cave. Follow it all the way through to {town}. Elder Maren will be waiting for you. Find her first.
Why: Earlier review (critic #11): arriving in town gave no goal; naming the elder points the player at her (the cave exit lands beside Maren).

Speaker: The Wanderer
Effective line: The trees close up that way. The cave, then.
Suggested line: The trees close up that way. The cave's back up the worn path, north-east of the camp.
Why: Folds in the earlier Critic #1 note: the stop line names the way to the cave.

Speaker: The Wanderer
Effective line: No point getting lost twice in one day. Back to the cave.
Suggested line: No point getting lost twice in one day. Back up the path to the glowing arch.
Why: Folds in the earlier note: names the landmark the player can actually see.

Speaker: Elder Maren
Effective line: Ten years ago {kingdom} was whole. Beefcakes made the energy, Gourmands fed us, Necrocrats minded the dead, Refusemancers hauled the waste and grew the crops.
Suggested line: Ten years ago {kingdom} was whole. Beefcakes made the energy, Gourmands fed us, Necrocrats minded the dead, Refusemancers hauled the waste and grew the crops. Everyone complained. Everything worked.
Why: A list becomes a Maren line with a sting, and seeds 'they argued and needed each other anyway'.

Speaker: Elder Maren
Effective line: Still here, dearie? The roads won't walk themselves. Well. Some of them would, if {villain} let them.
Suggested line: Still here, dearie? {villain} would love you to sit by my fire forever. Don't give him the satisfaction. Give me back my chair.
Why: The current 'some roads would walk themselves' turn doesn't land; this keeps the push out the door and ends on her sting.

Speaker: Sable
Effective line: You start with plain neutral cards. The Paths are where the power is. Browse, buy, then put it all to work at the Deck Station.
Suggested line: You start with plain neutral cards, darling: honest, dependable, dull. The Paths are where the power is. Buy some, then put them to work at the Deck Station.
Why: The tutorial line could be anyone's; 'darling' and a three-beat pitch make it Sable's.

Speaker: Tilly Tonic
Effective line: Potions and charms, back for more! Equip them on your Character screen for fights - maybe skip the orange one until I stop matching it!
Suggested line: Back for more potions! Equip them on your Character screen before a fight! Maybe skip the orange one until I stop matching it!
Why: 'Potions and charms, back for more!' reads as if the potions came back; same info, cleaner.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: Whatever it is, it is not open for business.
Suggested line: Whatever it is, it sounds like it has been on hold for a very long time.
Why: 'Not open for business' is used three times in town; this one sets up the ghosts' customer-service voice instead.

Speaker: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant to the Regional Merchant
Effective line: I will be here, guarding the drawer.
Suggested line: I will be here, guarding the drawer. The drawer does not know. That is the point.
Why: A bare closing line gets one deadpan Bertram turn.

Speaker: Announcer Grand Bellows
Effective line: Whatever is down there is not open for business. Yet.
Suggested line: Somewhere below, very faintly, someone is rehearsing the word CHAMPION. Not yet, apparently.
Why: Second 'not open for business'; this hints at Bellows before you meet him and keeps the 'not yet'.

Speaker: Auntie Alembic
Effective line: Whenever you collect more copies of a card than you can carry, the extras turn into essence of that card's Path.
Suggested line: When you collect more copies of a card than you can carry, dear, the extras boil down into essence of that card's Path. Nothing goes to waste here.
Why: Same rule, in Alembic's soft voice instead of a tooltip's.

Speaker: Pip Threadwell
Effective line: And the Capital's mantle... well. Someone has to defeat the person who owns it first.
Suggested line: And the Capital's mantle... well. Someone must defeat its owner first. The mantle, frankly, is rooting for you.
Why: Gives Pip's teaser his melodrama and a punchline instead of trailing off.

Speaker: Announcer Grand Bellows
Effective line: A champion who fights with every Path at once, and has a hand on every card. Bring your best deck.
Suggested line: A champion who fights with every Path at once, and has a fist for each. Bring your best deck.
Why: 'A hand on every card' is unclear; a fist per Path sets up the Fourth Fist event.

Speaker: Announcer Grand Bellows
Effective line: Another win for the books. The crowd roars (and tosses you some coins).
Suggested line: ANOTHER WIN FOR THE BOOKS! (normal voice) Some coins for you. From the crowd. The crowd is me.
Why: Puts the replay win in Bellows' loud-then-small voice; the coins stay.

Speaker: Announcer Grand Bellows
Effective line: The puzzle got the better of you. Study the board and try again.
Suggested line: THE PUZZLE WINS THIS ROUND! (normal voice) Study the board. Try again. It's not going anywhere.
Why: The only Bellows line with no Bellows in it; keeps the advice.

Speaker: Rip Tearson and cousins
Effective line: Walk into a town, and its station wakes up. Then you can rip between any two of them. Thank you for ripping with the Express.
Suggested line: After that, you can rip between any two stations. Thank you for ripping with the Express. Please keep your elbows inside the sky.
Why: The first half repeated the box before it; cut the repeat and give the sign-off a joke.

Speaker: Rip Tearson and cousins
Effective line: Spotter! Big news. You know that forest where you all started out?
Suggested line: Spotter! Big news. You know that forest outside town, where you first turned up?
Why: 'Where you all started out' reads oddly; this matches the station blurb.

Speaker: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant to the Regional Merchant
Effective line: Fact: bears cannot open the drawer. Nobody opens the drawer. Protocol One.
Suggested line: Fact: bears cannot open the drawer. Nobody opens the drawer. Protocol Three.
Why: Protocol One is already 'assess the customer's gait'; Three is unused.

Speaker: Auntie Alembic
Effective line: The flasks are humming today, dear. Don't touch the red one. It bites.
Suggested line: The flasks all bubbled when you passed, dear. Every colour. They never do that for me.
Why: Seeds the four-colours clue as a vendor noticing it without knowing why; the red flask joke lives on elsewhere.

Speaker: Brick Bronson (corrupted)
Effective line: Never lift alone. An old man told me that. Never broke, they say. Huh.
Suggested line: Never lift alone. An old man told me that. Haven't seen him in years. Huh.
Why: 'Never broke, they say' is hard to parse; this keeps the crack in Brick and points at Flex.

Speaker: Crosspath townsfolk
Effective line: Lovely day for a quest, isn't it? Shh. Not too lovely. Somebody's listening.
Suggested line: Say what you like about His Perfection, the wells are clean. Shh. Don't, actually.
Why: Swaps a generic 'lovely day for a quest' for Primm's real reform and the watched town in one bark.

Speaker: Brick Bronson
Effective line: The bridge is drawn up on the far side of the gorge. Somebody very large is standing by the crank.
Suggested line: The bridge is drawn up on the far side of the gorge. Somebody very large is standing by the crank, shouting about hydration.
Why: Introduces Brick by his tic before you meet him; the hook gets a laugh.

Speaker: Brick Bronson
Effective line: YOU WANT THE CRANK? EARN YOUR TURN - TEN REPS OF PAIN!
Suggested line: YOU WANT THE CRANK? TEN REPS! NO REST! I HAVE NOT SAT DOWN SINCE SPRING! IT IS GOING GREAT!
Why: Keeps the challenge but lets the zone's exhaustion leak through the hype.

Speaker: Brick Bronson
Effective line: NOBODY CROSSES THE GORGE WITHOUT A SPOTTER. I AM THE SPOTTER. SPOT THIS.
Suggested line: SPOTTERS ONLY. I AM SPOTTERS. ...SPOTTER. I AM ONE SPOTTER.
Why: The intro card repeated his first dialogue line word for word; this is the bible's stronger Brick joke.

Speaker: Brick Bronson
Effective line: HA! The pump is still MINE!
Suggested line: HA! THE PUMP IS STILL MINE! GO HOME AND HYDRATE! THAT IS AN ORDER, NOT CONCERN!
Why: The gentle giant shows through the corrupted shouting; sets up his freed self.

Speaker: Old Man Mountain
Effective line: "Passed out mid-rep. Happens to the best of us. Happened to me in the spring of... well. The tab's on you.
Suggested line: "Passed out mid-rep. Happens to the best of us. Happened to me in the spring of... the spring of... well. Towel's on your tab.
Why: Real Mountain trail-off, and the tab joke now pays off the very small towel in the box before.

Speaker: Throwers and rippers
Effective line: Shredna rolls her shoulders. "Calf Cove. Nobody's been out there in months.
Suggested line: Shredna rolls her shoulders. "Calf Cove. Did the old yeti say hello? ...Don't tell me. I don't care. Did he, though?
Why: Pays off Mountain's "She'll pretend she didn't miss me" and stops repeating his "nobody's been out there in months".

Speaker: Throwers and rippers
Effective line: No tools, just lats. I open doors by taking a very personal interest in the wall."
Suggested line: I don't open doors. I take a very personal interest in a wall until it gives up."
Why: Rita already says "No tools... just lats"; Ripley gets her own tic.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: Pushed by hand, by Beefcakes, since forever.
Suggested line: Pushed by hand, by Beefcakes, since forever. (The D.N.A. once asked for exact start times. We said "morning-ish".)
Why: Seeds the Beefcake-Necrocrat rivalry in one sign line.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: Run it to power the grid. No actual hamsters. Hamsters are on break.
Suggested line: Run it to power the grid. No actual hamsters. The hamsters get breaks.
Why: Same joke, but now it says the Beefcakes don't, which is the zone's problem.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: East to west. A courtesy chuck, the long way. Gym Rat card required for the long way.
Suggested line: East to west. A courtesy chuck, the long way. Gym Rat card required; Coach Benchley sells them.
Why: Cuts the repeated "the long way" and tells the player where to get the card.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: The regime's stronghold. Authorized personnel only.
Suggested line: The regime's stronghold. Authorized personnel only. Authorization takes thirty seconds, by order of the Minister of Efficiency.
Why: Plants Quota before her checkpoint scene, in her own unit of measure.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You see a regime enforcer flexing at nobody. Since breakfast, apparently; even his audience is exhausted.
Suggested line: You see a regime enforcer flexing at nobody. He has held the pose since breakfast, because nobody has told him he can stop.
Why: Fixes "at nobody" vs "his audience", and the joke now carries the exhaustion under the hype.

Speaker: Old Man Mountain
Effective line: Shh. Welcome to the Gainlands. The regime has ears. Big ones. I'm Old Man Mountain. We Beefcakes power the kingdom on mills and hamster wheels, and move folks by throw and by portal.
Suggested line: Shh. Welcome to the Gainlands. The regime has ears. Big ones. Old Man Mountain. We Beefcakes keep the kingdom's lights on and its folks moving. Wheels, mills... and if you're in a hurry, we throw you.
Why: Same Path facts in his voice instead of a brochure sentence; punchline last.

Speaker: Professor Pump
Effective line: Fifteen concern biceps; the regime burned the other two, so I rewrote them from memory. You cannot confiscate a well-trained brain-cep.
Suggested line: Fifteen concern biceps. The other two were a history of the Lifting Festival; the regime burned those, so I rewrote them from memory. You cannot confiscate a well-trained brain-cep.
Why: Says what the regime burned and why it matters: the festival and the old king, which Mountain then fills in.

Speaker: Professor Pump
Effective line: Answer well for gold and glory. Answer poorly and receive a mild, scholarly sigh. Today, we train the brain-ceps.
Suggested line: Answer well for gold and glory. Answer poorly and receive a mild, scholarly sigh. I have practised the sigh. It is devastating.
Why: Drops a second "brain-ceps" two boxes after the first and ends on a joke in his voice.

Speaker: Professor Pump
Effective line: Another lap! The Gainlands pay a small processing fee for repeat attendance.
Suggested line: Another lap! The Gainlands pay a little less for repeat attendance. The regime calls it a "processing fee". A D.N.A. phrase, I suspect.
Why: Says plainly that repeats pay less, and adds a rivalry jab in the Professor's footnote voice.

Speaker: Chet Thunderabs
Effective line: Not quite a set, champ. That's fine. Take a breath.
Suggested line: Not quite a set, champ! But WAIT - that wasn't a failure! That was a FREE TRIAL!
Why: Chet "never a quiet sentence": the loss line becomes an infomercial pitch.

Speaker: Gym attendant
Effective line: Gym's open! The weights are not. Regime orders. Enjoy the mirrors.
Suggested line: Gym's open! The weights are not. The scales stayed, though - standard measures, from the Capital. Say what you like, they never lie.
Why: A grudging nod to Primm's genuinely good reforms (standard measures), in an ambient line.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You receive an empty cup. The stand has mistaken protein for a serving suggestion.
Suggested line: You receive an empty cup. Flavour: surprise.
Why: Calls back the stand's own sign ("Flavour: surprise.") instead of a joke that does not quite land.

Speaker: Foreman Gus
Effective line: The Swole Station's lights are back on, and the grid's HUMMING. Take your reward before I turn this into a pep talk.
Suggested line: The Swole Station's lights are back on. Grid's humming. I'd make a speech, but all my energy went into the lights. Take your reward.
Why: Gus is flat and tired; "HUMMING" and a pep-talk threat read like Benchley.

Speaker: Coach Brutus Benchley
Effective line: Regime brutes, golems and sprites keep eating my deliveries! Beat any three roaming enemies in the Gainlands in card duels - END THE BULKING ORDERS!
Suggested line: Regime brutes, golems and sprites keep eating my deliveries! Beat any three roaming enemies in the Gainlands in card duels! THOSE SHAKES HAD MY NAME ON THEM!
Why: "END THE BULKING ORDERS" was unclear; this keeps the instruction and the coach volume.

Speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
Effective line: Just measuring. Lovely broad shoulders round here. Very roomy work. Heh.
Suggested line: Just measuring. Lovely broad shoulders round here. Very roomy work, when it comes. It hasn't, lately. Heh.
Why: A quiet hint that Death is stuck, funny only once you know who Hob is.

Speaker: Baron Quadzilla, the Leg Press Lord
Effective line: Baron Quadzilla racks the plates, stands, and wobbles. 'Huh,' he says. 'Standing. Wobbly. Like a first rep.'
Suggested line: Baron Quadzilla racks the plates, stands, and wobbles. 'Huh,' he says, looking down. 'So those are my feet. Hello, feet.'
Why: The old line repeated his mid-fight bark word for word; this gives the payoff its own joke.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: Rows of lockers hold the old champions' gear, every strap labelled by weight class. A laminated sign reads LOCKER 13 IS A STATE OF MIND. One door hangs ajar, humming the theme from a boxing movie.
Suggested line: Rows of lockers hold the old champions' gear, every strap labelled by weight class. A laminated sign reads LOCKER 13 IS A STATE OF MIND. One door hangs ajar, humming a training-montage tune to itself.
Why: "A boxing movie" is a real-world reference that breaks the setting; same joke without it.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: Every weight the regime ever took. Behind a locker door, and behind a very sad sign.
Suggested line: Every weight the regime ever took, stacked behind one locker door. Each plate still has its owner's name chalked on the back.
Why: Turns a flat line into a small human detail: these weights belong to people and are waiting to go home.

Speaker: Grandmaster Flex
Effective line: The rounds are irregular. Listen for them on the stairs.
Suggested line: Their squats are not regular, so neither are the rounds. Listen for the knees on the stairs.
Why: Fixes the clash with "time their rounds by their squats" and gives Flex a calm punchline.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You read the plate on the empty pedestal: GRANDMASTER FLEX (PENDING). The space above it remains empty.
Suggested line: You read the plate on the empty pedestal: GRANDMASTER FLEX (PENDING). It has been dusted. Recently.
Why: "Empty... remains empty" said the same thing twice; the dusting shows how sure the regime is.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: No spotter needed on the roof. He is holding that pose for himself.
Suggested line: Wave, and he will wave back. After the pose. The pose may take a while.
Why: Gives the freed Flex sign a joke in his patient, unhurried style.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: (Town. Stairs sold separately. The cardio checkpoint has been repurposed as a snack bar.)
Suggested line: (To town. The cardio checkpoint is a snack bar now. Snacks are mandatory.)
Why: "Stairs sold separately" was unclear; the freed zone now uses the regime's word warmly.

Speaker: Old Man Mountain
Effective line: YOU DID IT. Flex is out, Clench is down, and I got to watch. Best day since... since the last best day. I'll be spotting you for the rest of your HP, like it or not.
Suggested line: YOU DID IT. Flex is out, Clench is down, and I got to watch. Best day since... since the last best day. I'm spotting you from now on, like it or not.
Why: Drops the gamey "rest of your HP"; keeps the warmth.

Speaker: Grandmaster Flex, the Unbroken
Effective line: Clench is learning to lift from zero. The strongest take the longest. The gym is open to everyone now. Come whenever you like.
Suggested line: Clench is learning to lift from zero. The strongest take the longest. Yesterday he spotted Gary without being asked. The gym is open to everyone now; come whenever you like.
Why: Shows Clench's first step back instead of only stating it, and pays off Gary.

Speaker: Chef Fennel Gravois, Keeper of the Pantry Key
Effective line: The great pantry door swings open. Somewhere beyond, something smells incredible.
Suggested line: The great pantry door swings open. Somewhere beyond, something smells incredible. Underneath it, faintly, something smells of hot iron.
Why: Plants the arms-factory secret on the very first step in, without a word of exposition.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: Your HP is full, and the chef says there are no seconds. You both know this is a serving of fiction.
Suggested line: Your HP is already full. A chef refills your plate anyway. Here, being full is treated as a misunderstanding.
Why: The current joke is muddled; this one comes straight from the zone's 'nobody leaves hungry' culture.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: A hidden stash! Nobody tasted that one. Lettuce rejoice.
Suggested line: A hidden stash! Unsampled, unsauced and all yours.
Why: The Pantry Run summary already spends the lettuce pun; this nods to the Special Sauce instead.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You fell in the gravy! Somebody fishes you out and sets you on dry ground. (-1 HP)
Suggested line: You fall in the gravy. A passing chef fishes you out with a ladle and checks you for seasoning. (-1 HP)
Why: Present tense like the rest of the narration, and a chef-shaped joke instead of 'Somebody'.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: The golem steps aside. The way is open.
Suggested line: The golem steps aside with the slow dignity of a roast being carved. The way is open.
Why: A flat system line gets one image of the knightly meat golems.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You ladle some soup. Delicious, but you are already stuffed to the brim.
Suggested line: You ladle some soup, look at it, and pour it back. You are full. The fountain takes it well.
Why: Replaces a plain statement with a small, deadpan beat.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: - Guard the kingdom (with golems)
Suggested line: - Guard the kingdom (with golems. Defensive golems. Please stop saying the other word.)
Why: The brief's 'chefs flinch at the word weapon' finally appears on the zone's first sign.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: Welcome to the far side. The gates ahead are guarded by golems, as is the custom.
Suggested line: Welcome to the far side. The gates ahead are guarded by golems, as is the custom. One wants saffron, one wants a favour, one wants a fight.
Why: Tells the player the three gate conditions at a glance, in sign rhythm.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: Please do not bite the buildings. They are load-bearing cake.
Suggested line: Please do not bite the buildings. The mayor's house is down to two layers, and he knows it was a visitor.
Why: 'Load-bearing' is Bertram's owned gag; this keeps the joke local to cake town.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: Four ingredients, in the right order, tastes like victory.
Suggested line: Four ingredients, in the right order. Anything else tastes like a lesson.
Why: The current sentence does not parse; this reads cleanly and keeps the hint.

Speaker: Basil
Effective line: Psst. Hello. I'm Basil, line cook. Ladle in one hand, nerves in the other. We Gourmands feed the kingdom and protect it. Every plate is a promise. Every golem is a guard.
Suggested line: Psst. Basil, line cook. Ladle in one hand, nerves in the other. We Gourmands feed the kingdom and protect it: chefs cook, golems guard. Lately the golems have been... practising.
Why: Swaps two poster slogans for a nervous hint of the war programme; Basil's voice, same fact.

Speaker: Sous-Chef Tarragon
Effective line: Don't tell the Grand Chef I said anything. She hears everything. She just never tastes anything.
Suggested line: Don't tell the Grand Chef I said anything. Last cook who complained got promoted to taste tester. We haven't seen him since.
Why: Basil already does 'hears everything, never tastes'; this gives Tarragon his own fear and pays off the taste-tester signs.

Speaker: Sous-Chef Tarragon
Effective line: I'm hungry and a bit scared. If either came with a side dish, we'd be sorted.
Suggested line: I'm so hungry I looked at a Refusemancer compost heap and thought 'starter'. Don't tell anyone. I'd never live it down.
Why: Uses the Gourmand vs 'garbage eaters' rivalry from someone sincerely inside the culture.

Speaker: Madame Mirepoix
Effective line: Gourmand-issue, inspected by the Test Kitchen as of this year. The stamp is on the decorative cake, which has never looked more unappetizing.
Suggested line: Gourmand-issue, inspected by the Test Kitchen as of this year. They stamped my decorative cake. Right on the rosette. I have not forgiven them.
Why: The current line is hard to follow; this keeps the stamp and sets up the cake with snoot.

Speaker: Sous-Chef Tarragon
Effective line: The pantry's stocked until tomorrow, when we do it all again. Fetching has a wonderful sense of repetition; I'd like to send it back.
Suggested line: The pantry's stocked until tomorrow, when we do it all again. I'm not complaining. I'm fetching. They look similar from a distance.
Why: The 'send it back' turn is muddled; this is cleaner overworked-intern panic.

Speaker: Madame Mirepoix
Effective line: One Hearty Pot Pie, darling. Honey, basil and a ghost pepper into the Grand Oven by the arch. I shall wait. I have cake.
Suggested line: One Hearty Pot Pie, darling. Honey, basil and a ghost pepper into the Grand Oven by the arch. I shall wait. I have a cake to look at.
Why: Her cake is decorative; the tweak lands her running gag and its later payoff.

Speaker: Professor Pate
Effective line: Back to improve your score? Splendid. Knowledge, like a good roux, wants patience. And butter. Mostly butter.
Suggested line: Back for more? Splendid. A footnote, while it simmers: the Capital's school lunches were excellent once. Hot, free, balanced. Then came the paste.
Why: Repeats his bark almost word for word; this works in Primm's genuinely good reform and Crumb's paste.

Speaker: (gate golem)
Effective line: The golem stands firm.
Suggested line: The golem stands firm, like an aspic that has made up its mind.
Why: One food image for a bare system line.

Speaker: Colonel Casserole
Effective line: En garde, traveller. A duel of honour. Lids up. Yes, Chef.
Suggested line: En garde! Thirty years of service, and I have never once boiled over. Until now. Yes, Chef.
Why: The event line nearly repeats his intro; this gives the half-health turn its own beat.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You find rations, ladles and ladle-shaped weapons. Take what you can carry; someone has overthought serving suggestions.
Suggested line: You find rations, ladles and ladle-shaped weapons in crates marked SERVING UTENSILS (DEFENSIVE). Take what you can carry.
Why: The euphemism is the zone's joke engine; the golems own 'overthought' ladles.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: Great vats of the Special Sauce bubble in the dark. This is where the corruption is made.
Suggested line: Great vats of the Special Sauce bubble in the dark. A clipboard on the rail reads: BATCH 3,652. TASTED BY: (blank).
Why: Shows the corruption instead of telling it: ten years of daily batches, nobody tasting.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: Blueprints, recipe cards and signed memos fill the cabinets. Every handwritten note signed by the Grand Chef leans the wrong way, as if written by someone who has only ever read about left-handedness.
Suggested line: Blueprints, recipe cards and signed memos fill the cabinets. Every note signed by the Grand Chef is in perfect copperplate, without one gravy stain. Real chefs' notes are mostly gravy stain.
Why: Turns the clunky left-handed clue into the zone's theme: appearance over substance.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: - Guard the kingdom (with golems)
Suggested line: - Guard the kingdom (with golems; the cannons are ovens now)
Why: The freed sign shows the zone has changed instead of repeating the old line.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: To {town}, through the great pantry door. Wipe your feet - we just mopped, but your sample is yours now; take two.
Suggested line: To {town}, through the great pantry door. Wipe your feet; we just mopped. Free samples by the door. Take two. Nobody is checking.
Why: The current line is tangled; this shows the freedom in plain sign rhythm.

Speaker: Sous-Chef Tarragon
Effective line: Tarragon! Sous-Chef! Free!
Suggested line: Tarragon! Sous-Chef! Fetcher of things! I caught up with lunch!
Why: Pays off his running gag of never catching up with lunch.

Speaker: (narration/UI)
Effective line: Official likeness withdrawn. It never captured the person who fed us.
Suggested line: Official likeness withdrawn. It never captured the person who fed us. (Also: whose chin is that?)
Why: Restores the 'Whose chin is that?' half of the chin gag pair the voice bible flags for restore.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You are already as rested as the dead get. Which is very rested. Technically, eternally.
Suggested line: You are already as rested as the dead get, and the dead get very rested.
Why: Cuts the tail that explains the joke.

Speaker: D.N.A. staff
Effective line: Parking Lot D has been renamed Parking Lot Dead. Please stop asking why.
Suggested line: Beefcake couriers: throwing a parcel through the window is not 'delivery'. Neither is throwing the courier.
Why: A weak pun replaced by the Necrocrat-Beefcake rivalry, filed as a memo.

Speaker: Gerald, Number 4,000,212
Effective line: Per my last email: still serving 3. I don't have email. I hope the phrase conveys that I have asked before.
Suggested line: Per my last memo: still serving 3. Per the memo before that: also 3.
Why: Keeps the 'per my last' weariness without stopping to explain the joke.

Speaker: Agnes Overdue
Effective line: Back again? Loyalty is rewarded here. Not with money. With more work.
Suggested line: Back again, dear? Nobody else leaves. Since the transfer, not one soul has passed on. Not even me.
Why: Generic workplace gag swapped for the zone's key fact (Death froze) in Agnes's own want.

Speaker: Agnes Overdue
Effective line: The Records Basement elevator needs Form 13-B. I don't have one. Nobody does. It builds character.
Suggested line: The Records Basement elevator needs Form 13-B. I don't have one. Nobody does. I applied, but the application form is a 13-B.
Why: 'It builds character' is filler; the loop of forms is the zone's own joke.

Speaker: Director Ectomund
Effective line: Re-certified again. The Department pays a small processing fee for the paperwork.
Suggested line: Re-certified again. For the paperwork, the Department pays you a small processing fee. It has never paid in that direction before.
Why: Makes clear the fee goes to the player, with a dry turn at the end.

Speaker: Director Ectomund
Effective line: Try again. The signs aren't going anywhere. Neither, technically, is anyone here.
Suggested line: Try again. The signs aren't going anywhere. Since the transfer, neither is anyone here.
Why: Same joke, now carrying why nobody here can leave.

Speaker: Director Ectomund
Effective line: One correct. Your token. My interest remains non-refundable.
Suggested line: One correct. Your token. I have noted your potential in the margin, in very small writing.
Why: 'My interest remains non-refundable' does not quite parse; this is the examiner's drone with a turn.

Speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
Effective line: I took a number. Heh. It's a big one.
Suggested line: I took a number. Heh. Makes a change. Usually I'm the one calling them.
Why: An Old Hob line that is funny now and funnier once you know who he is.

Speaker: Kyle (Deceased Since '09)
Effective line: brb, haunting. actually stay. nobody reads the 'be right back' part.
Suggested line: brb, haunting. been brb since '09. it's a long b.
Why: The current bark is muddled; this is one clean Kyle joke.

Zone/Area: D.N.A. / The Waiting Room of Eternity
Speaker: Betty Bones, Surly Secretary
Effective line: Take a number. The number is irrelevant. Take it anyway.
Suggested line: Take a number. I won't be calling it. Take it anyway.
Why: 'Irrelevant' is Mortimer's word; this is Betty's never-impressed shrug.

Zone/Area: D.N.A. / The Hall of Final Approvals
Speaker: Agnes Overdue
Effective line: Agnes Overdue. Front desk, and on my lunch hour, appellant. I stopped counting the appeals. Every one denied.
Suggested line: Agnes Overdue. Front desk, and on my lunch hour, appellant. Forty thousand appeals, every one denied. They've started decorating the stamps.
Why: 'I stopped counting' contradicts her bark (appeal forty thousand and one); she keeps the receipts.

Zone/Area: D.N.A. / The Hall of Final Approvals
Speaker: D.N.A. staff
Effective line: Every important document in the Hall passes through here. It must be stamped, signed and witnessed by a notary.
Suggested line: Every important document in the Hall is stamped, signed and witnessed here. The transfer of authority was, too. The notary is still finding blue-green feathers.
Why: A quiet clue to Plume, the peacock who notarized the transfer, before the player meets him.

Speaker: Kyle
Effective line: the queue moved. like, actually moved. my number's coming up in only four hundred years. new personal best.
Suggested line: the queue moved. like, actually moved. agnes called my number at 3am. i was afk. she called it again. nobody's ever called me twice.
Why: The current line says his number is 400 years off, which contradicts Agnes calling every number the night the zone is freed.

Speaker: Director Ectomund
Effective line: Back again. The Department has reopened its records to honest examination, so I examine with a clear conscience now.
Suggested line: Back again. The ethics questions have been returned to the building. Not yet to the exam. One reform at a time.
Why: Pays off his own setup (ethics removed, 'not in the building') instead of a flat statement.

Speaker: Agnes Overdue
Effective line: Head of the whole Department, and still on the front desk. Old habits, dear. Ghosts were never good at being in one place.
Suggested line: Head of the whole Department, and still on the front desk. They gave me a big office, dear. Nobody waits in a big office. They wait here.
Why: The ghost line did not follow; this says why she stays at the desk, which is her whole arc.

Speaker: Moss Mulligan, the Corrupted Druid
Effective line: The Rot took Archdruid Compostella first, at the Rotheart, deep in the Verdant Dump. Everything else grew out from her.
Suggested line: The Rot took Archdruid Compostella first, at the Rotheart, deep in the Verdant Dump. Everything grew out from her. Me too, the day a very tidy lady with shears came calling.
Why: Plants Clipwell (who corrupted Moss) before the mill, in Moss's shy voice.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You eat roast roots and a pie with a crust like a fence post. The mug is mostly apple. You are thoroughly farm-fed. HP restored.
Suggested line: You eat roast roots and a pie with a crust like a fence post. The mug is mostly apple. A goat watches every bite. HP restored.
Why: Replaces a flat third beat with the zone's goat gag; works before and after freeing.

Speaker: Dump workers
Effective line: New stairs. Same climb. I was hoping they would fix that.
Suggested line: New stairs. Same climb. And the stairs grew two more steps overnight.
Why: Puts the never-stops-growing wrongness into a worker grumble; keeps the freed pair's opening.

Speaker: Dump workers
Effective line: Every terrace a little higher, every terrace a little weirder. That's the Dump for you.
Suggested line: The Buffet calls us garbage eaters. Half our garbage is their souffle, barely touched.
Why: Seeds the Gourmand rivalry from inside the zone; the old line was filler.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: The belt has never lost a piece of sleep over your performance.
Suggested line: The belt does not slow down for anyone. It has been asked.
Why: The old idiom was garbled; this is cleaner and lands on a joke.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: A pile of tyres, doors and ambition across the gap.
Suggested line: A pile of tyres, doors and one very stubborn wardrobe across the gap.
Why: "Ambition" is the third junk-pile ambition in the zone; a concrete object is funnier.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: A trash golem towers over you, moss coating its fridge body. Something sprouts from its ears. This is no place for a cool head.
Suggested line: A trash golem towers over you, moss coating its fridge body. Something sprouts from its ears. Inside, the little light is still on.
Why: "Cool head" is the Buffet golems' owned pun; the fridge-light image is the Dump's own joke.

Speaker: Brother Bramble
Effective line: We are the Refusemancers: druids of waste removal and agriculture. Our animals eat the kingdom's garbage and turn it into fertilizer, and our magic helps the crops grow.
Suggested line: We are the Refusemancers: druids of waste removal and agriculture. Our animals turn the kingdom's garbage into fertilizer for its crops. The Buffet calls us garbage eaters. They eat our carrots.
Why: Same facts, shorter, plus the rivalry and why the Paths need each other, punchline last.

Speaker: Granny Gristle
Effective line: Shop's open, dearie! Turnips are a day old. A lovely vintage, if you're a turnip.
Suggested line: Back again, dearie! Turnips are a day old. A lovely vintage, if you're a turnip.
Why: Retires the generic "Shop's open" greeting; keeps the vintage turnip gag.

Speaker: Wren Muckfoot
Effective line: The boar and goat in the stables will carry you. Ask nicely. Ask rudely. They don't speak either. Good, sensible animals.
Suggested line: The boar and goat in the stables will carry you. Ask nicely or ask rudely; they ignore both the same. Good, sensible animals.
Why: "They don't speak either" reads as a contradiction right after "I speak fluent goat".

Zone/Area: Verdant Dump / The Trash Panda Throne
Speaker: His Majesty the Raccoon
Effective line: 'WE DID NOT EAT THE COMPOST. We sampled it.' His Majesty grips the throne. 'The royal tasting is not open to questions.'
Suggested line: 'WE DID NOT EAT THE COMPOST. We... sampled it.' His Majesty grips the throne. 'The royal tasting is not open to questions.'
Why: Restores the canon catchphrase's pause ("We... sampled it").

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: Normal-looking plants, mostly. They are a little too green. Everything is alive in a way that feels like it is watching you.
Suggested line: Normal-looking plants, mostly. A little too green. Every leaf turns, very slightly, to follow you.
Why: Shows the watching instead of telling the player how it feels.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: The vines are choosing who gets through. Can your deck keep its footing?
Suggested line: The vines are choosing who gets through. They are reading your deck very closely.
Why: "Footing" is Coach Benchley's owned pun.

Speaker: Hortensia Clipwell, Royal Groundskeeper
Effective line: Such a pretty weed. Such a shame. Now, stand still while I tidy you.
Suggested line: Gentlemen, if you would. He is well over regulation height.
Why: Was a word-for-word repeat of her intro line; now she sends the topiaries in with her regulation-height tic.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: It tastes of rain and regret. You feel hardier, and a little poisoned.
Suggested line: It tastes of rain and old boots. You feel hardier, and a little poisoned.
Why: "Rain and regret" repeats the mushroom result; the boot calls back the pool's own text.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: A tunnel full of drifting spores. Whether you can walk through it depends on how well your deck has been built.
Suggested line: A tunnel of drifting spores. A well-built deck walks straight through. A loose one starts to sprout.
Why: Same hint, with a turn at the end instead of a rules sentence.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You see light pour through the splitting Rotheart.
Suggested line: Light pours through the splitting Rotheart.
Why: Drops the flat "You see" camera narration the review flagged.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You watch wildflowers follow the light outward through the Dump.
Suggested line: Wildflowers follow the light outward, field by field, through the Dump.
Why: Drops "You watch"; one concrete image.

Speaker: Granny Gristle
Effective line: Shop's open! Day-old turnips. None looking at anybody. Finally, produce that knows when to look away. Heh!
Suggested line: Day-old turnips, dearie, and not one of them looking at anybody. Finally, produce with manners. Heh!
Why: Retires "Shop's open" and tightens the turnip payoff.

Speaker: Compostella, the Rotheart, and Archdruid Compostella
Effective line: Archdruid Compostella. I am told what happened to the barn. I cannot remember doing it. I will help put it right.
Suggested line: Archdruid Compostella. I am told what happened to the barn. I cannot remember doing it. The barn, I gather, remembers me. I will help put it right.
Why: Lands her canon barn gag (she forgets, it remembers); her bark already offers to mend it.

Speaker: Elder Maren
Effective line: You have earned the truth. I have been keeping more from you than I should.
Suggested line: You have earned the truth, so here is the first piece of it: I am not only a tortoise who bakes.
Why: Restores Maren's own turn into the confession; the current line says she is hiding things instead of showing it.

Speaker: Elder Maren
Effective line: I wasn't sure I could trust you before. I am now.
Suggested line: I wasn't sure of you before. I am sure now. Mostly.
Why: Restores her sting in the tail; 'Mostly.' is pure Maren and keeps her guarded at stage 2.

Speaker: Elder Maren
Effective line: I have been hiding here ever since.
Suggested line: I have been hiding here ever since, with my hands in pie dough, where nobody would ask what else they had made.
Why: Gives the bare line a concrete, sincere image: the pie was where she hid the hands that blew the glass.

Speaker: Elder Maren
Effective line: One Path left under {villain}'s thumb. The whole town is holding its breath. It's murder on my knees.
Suggested line: One Path left under {villain}'s thumb. The whole town is holding its breath. I can hold mine for a week. They cannot.
Why: The knees joke does not follow from holding breath; a tortoise who can hold hers all week does.

Speaker: Elder Maren
Effective line: The roads are open. Even the tortoises use them. I passed one this morning. Barely.
Suggested line: The roads are open. Even I use them. I passed a hare this morning. He has asked for a recount.
Why: Earlier review (Oct 28): Maren is a tortoise again, so 'the tortoises use them' reads oddly; the joke moves onto her.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You find a boot in the spring. Clear water slips around its heel. Even here, something finds a way through.
Suggested line: Someone has thrown a boot in the spring. The water has gone politely round it.
Why: Restores the dry running gag (the water going politely round the boot) and drops the platitude.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You recall the first words of every Gourmand recipe: first, water. Someone has added 'and salt' here. Twice.
Suggested line: Every Gourmand recipe still begins with the same two words: first, water. Somebody has added 'and salt' here. Twice.
Why: Drops the 'You recall' frame; the player cannot recall a recipe, the narration can state it.

Speaker: The Wanderer
Effective line: A well with opinions. I'll take a bottle's worth.
Suggested line: A well with opinions. Fine. I'm keeping the bottle.
Why: Restores the Wanderer's version (story bible): 'Fine.' is his undercut, and 'keeping' lands the joke.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: The service-tunnel network is down. Nobody has run the wheels that power the shaft lifts in ten years. 'No travel,' says a Wrinkle's note on the hatch.
Suggested line: The service-tunnel network is down. The wheels that once turned the shaft lifts have spent ten years lighting the facade instead. 'No travel,' says a Wrinkle's note on the hatch.
Why: The current line says nobody runs the wheels, in a district built on wheels that never stop; this squares it and shows where the power went.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: A real recipe, written by hand, with a stain of actual sauce on the corner! A pinch of this, a spoonful of that. It is wonderfully imprecise. You tuck it away.
Suggested line: A real recipe, written by hand, with a stain of actual sauce on the corner! Flour: some. Salt: enough. Time: until it smells right. It is wonderfully imprecise. You tuck it away.
Why: Uses Chef Marlo's 'some' quantities so the card reads as his, with a sharper picture of the imprecision.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: The second wheel has been turning since before some of its runners were old enough to vote. A foreman's whistle hangs from a hook. You take it off its hook and put it in your pocket.
Suggested line: The second wheel has been turning since some of its runners were too small to reach the pedals. A foreman's whistle hangs from a hook. You pocket it.
Why: Drops 'old enough to vote' (odd in a monarchy) and the doubled hook; the image does the work.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: The third wheel's crew are children. Children! 'It is a school activity,' says a banner.
Suggested line: The third wheel's crew are children in school caps. 'It is a school activity,' says a banner. Nobody has rung the bell.
Why: Narration shows instead of exclaiming 'Children!'; the bell that never rings carries the horror quietly.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You watch the neighbourhood carry Mr. Pell to his grave. A quiet tune accompanies the coffin as they lower it.
Suggested line: You watch the neighbourhood carry Mr. Pell to his grave. Nobody holds a permit to sing, so they sing very quietly. Nobody stops them.
Why: Replaces the vague 'a quiet tune accompanies' with one specific, sincere act of small defiance; no joke on the beat.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: The Beefcakes kept the kingdom's energy and its roads: the wheels, the mills, the throwers and the portal-rippers. {villain} put them all on wheels to light one small town. The rest of the kingdom went dark.
Suggested line: The Beefcakes kept the kingdom's energy and its roads: the wheels, the mills, the throwers and the portal-rippers. {villain} put them all on wheels to light one showpiece street. The rest of the kingdom went dark.
Why: 'One small town' in narration can read as the hub town; the facade is one showpiece street.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: A Showcase Quarter, built to show what the whole kingdom could be if everybody simply tried harder.
Suggested line: Every house in this quarter was built to show what the whole kingdom could be if everybody simply tried harder.
Why: The line spells the district name literally in a story file (token rule) and the sign need not repeat its own heading.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: To the Crease. The dead are not allowed down. The living are a little afraid of the dead down there. Be kind.
Suggested line: To the Crease. Living passengers only. The dead have asked to come down too; we are thinking about it. Be kind.
Why: The current sign contradicts itself (the dead are not allowed down, yet the living fear the dead down there); this is clear and funnier.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: The Paths tear where {villain} forced them into one shape. His hold is failing; the tears began the night someone escaped the Ministry.
Suggested line: The tears are temporary and fully under control. (Scrawled below: the Paths tear where {villain} forced them into one shape. His hold slipped the night someone escaped the Ministry.)
Why: An official sign would never admit his hold is failing; the fact survives as a Wrinkle's scrawl under the slogan, the Capital's core joke.

Speaker: Wren
Effective line: Back in one piece? Good. Mostly one piece.
Suggested line: Back in one piece? Good. Hesper charges by the piece.
Why: Wren's one sharp joke per scene, and a nod to Hesper's correction fee, instead of a repeated 'one piece'.

Speaker: Wren
Effective line: The records say he began as a good man. Keep that in mind. It does not excuse what he has done.
Suggested line: The records say he began well. His first decree put a hot lunch in front of every schoolchild. Remember that. It excuses nothing.
Why: The archivist is the natural voice for Primm's sincere early reforms; one concrete good deed makes him tragic before the castle.

Speaker: Widow Pell
Effective line: I talk to him in the parlour. I don't know what else to do. Please, if you can help.
Suggested line: I talk to him in the parlour. He was always the patient one. I'm not, it turns out. Please, if you can help.
Why: Gives Pell her own soft dry humour about herself, never at her loss, and keeps the plea.

Speaker: Captain Spotless
Effective line: I have measured eleven thousand visitors. I approved four. Nine thousand were sent home. The rest, I will not say.
Suggested line: I have measured twelve thousand visitors. I approved four. Nine thousand were sent home. The rest, I will not say.
Why: 'Eleven' is the prince's story clue; a gate tally should not spend it casually. Same joke, same shape.

Speaker: Capital guards and clerks
Effective line: Still above regulation. Still letting it go. Do not make me regret it.
Suggested line: Still one hair above regulation. I have thought about that hair all week. Do not make me regret it.
Why: Pays off his 'one hair' from the intro and shows a small human obsession instead of repeating 'still'.

Speaker: Rollo Spokes
Effective line: Here. From the old days: what we gave people who could keep going.
Suggested line: Here... from the old days. We gave these out... at the end of a shift. Remember ends?
Why: Breathless Rollo rhythm, a clearer reward line, and the quest's whole point (stopping) as the punchline.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Effective line: Everyone is so friendly! Everyone is so friendly. It is like living inside a greeting card.
Suggested line: Everyone is so friendly! Everyone is so friendly. It is like living inside a greeting card. The kind with nothing written in it.
Why: One more clause turns a flat simile into the slogan-and-whisper gap.

Speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
Effective line: Please continue to be happy, as scheduled! This has been your Deputy Minister of Good News!
Suggested line: Please continue to be happy, as scheduled! Lost Ministry property must be returned at once, and not spoken to!
Why: Puts the 'escaped Royal Asset' hunt into the broadcasts; 'not spoken to' is funny early and chilling after the reveal.

Speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
Effective line: Attention, citizens! Please remember: the exits are for ENTERING. The entrances are for EXITING.
Suggested line: Great news, citizens! The public records have never been tidier! Every untidy page has been corrected!
Why: The exit-is-the-entrance joke is already the exit guard's; this spends the broadcast on tidy records curdling into erased history, which sets up Wren.

Speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
Effective line: Anything else is an unapproved Direction.
Suggested line: If you remember things differently, please report to the Correction Ward. Your memory will be tidied too!
Why: Second box of the records broadcast: Plume's cheer over a real threat, pointing at a place the player can visit.

Speaker: Vivienne Quota, Minister of Efficiency
Effective line: You. Again. You cost me the Gainlands in four hours and eleven minutes. I have had the figure framed.
Suggested line: You. Again. You cost me the Gainlands in four hours and twelve minutes. I have had the figure framed.
Why: 'Eleven' is a story clue; Quota's precision works with any figure.

Speaker: Old Fern
Effective line: Granny Gristle needs hands on the compost rows down in the Dump. Peel from shell. Messy work.
Suggested line: Granny Gristle needs hands on the compost rows down in the Dump. Sorting peel from shell, all day. Messy. You'll hate it. Good.
Why: 'Peel from shell' reads as a typo; this is clear and gives Fern her grumbly last word over the tidy hare.

Speaker: Rollo Spokes
Effective line: Trained with... the Gainlands wheel crews. They told us... it was cardio.
Suggested line: Back in the Gainlands... we threw commuters. Now I'd pay... to be thrown.
Why: His other lines already say 'it was cardio'; this adds the Beefcakes' people-throwing transport and an exhausted joke.

Zone/Area: The Capital / The Old Service Tunnels
Speaker: (narration/UI)
Effective line: The junction crew trains on scrap: tyre flips, bin presses, dumbbells made of drain pipe. Every Garbage becomes muscle.
Suggested line: Beefcake bore, Gourmand vents, Necrocrat signs, Refusemancer drains. The junction crew lifts the scrap. Every Garbage becomes muscle.
Why: The Four-Faction Junction is the place to show the tunnels were built by all four Paths together; keeps the Garbage-to-muscle hint.

Speaker: Colonel Cornelius Crumb, Director of Culinary Defense
Effective line: HALT! This is a restricted pantry! Those recipes are confiscated for the war effort!
Suggested line: ATTENTION! This is a restricted pantry! Those recipes are confiscated for the war effort!
Why: HALT is Captain Spotless's catchphrase; Crumb barks drill-sergeant orders.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: 'Welcome,' says a quiet voice. 'Please wipe your feet. You are expected.'
Suggested line: 'Welcome,' says a quiet, polite voice from nowhere. 'Please wipe your feet. Please wipe your opinions. You are expected.'
Why: Restores the flagged 'wipe your opinions': Primm's polish in one clause, before he appears.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: 'All Gourmands to be fed the sauce. They will be happier. They will no longer need to choose for themselves.'
Suggested line: All Gourmands to be fed the sauce. They will be happier, and a little less themselves. I consider this the improvement.'
Why: Restores the flagged 'less themselves' beat in Primm's precise clipboard voice; also drops a stray second opening quote mid-note.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: 'When the champion is weak, he will no longer be a disagreement. NOTE: he continues to train without the weights. Observe carefully.'
Suggested line: When the champion is sufficiently weak, he will no longer be a disagreement. NOTE: do not underestimate him. He does a lot of stretching.'
Why: Restores the story bible's own quote (precision that is accidentally funny) and drops a stray opening quote; the margin note then answers it.

Speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
Effective line: Great news, citizens! The traitor has been located!
Suggested line: Great news, citizens! The traitor has been located! Please hold your applause until she has been removed.
Why: Plume's spin gets its turn: the slogan over the arrest.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You see a curator patrol the side gallery, feather duster in hand. He straightens each frame without looking at its face. (A battle.)
Suggested line: A curator with a feather duster patrols the side gallery. Anything crooked, he straightens. Anything alive, he dusts. (A battle.)
Why: Restores the flagged 'Anything alive, he dusts' and drops the 'You see' narration.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You face a clerk at a tall desk. His stamp falls rapidly; his eyes stay on the paper. (A battle.)
Suggested line: A clerk at a tall desk, stamping everything that moves. Quite fast. Quite sad. His eyes never leave the paper. (A battle.)
Why: Restores 'Quite fast. Quite sad.' (flagged) while keeping the tested 'His eyes'.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You face a vast staircase. Every step is the same height; you cannot see the landing from the bottom. A story event.
Suggested line: A staircase so grand it has its own staircase. Every step is exactly the same height; you cannot see the landing from the bottom. A story event.
Why: Restores the flagged image; 'You face a vast staircase' is placeholder narration.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You leave the cracked dome behind and return to the hall.
Suggested line: You leave the seed where it fell. Out of its dome it looks smaller. Most things here do. You go back.
Why: Gives the wing a closing image (his works shrink once looked at) instead of a bare exit line.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You sit in the reading chair. One person has worn a hollow in its seat. Beside you, lamplight shines through a handmade shade.
Suggested line: You sit in the old reading chair. It is worn exactly where one person sat, every night, for years. Someone made the lampshade by hand. It is a little crooked.
Why: Puts back the flagged human detail and ends on 'crooked', the game's word for freedom, in Primm's own room.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You follow the lines of the plans with one finger. Then you roll up the best and take it. Your throat tightens.
Suggested line: They are good. They are so good. You roll up the best and take it, with something in your throat.
Why: Restores the flagged 'They are so good' motif: Primm began as a good man.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You remove the old gold frame. The mirror remains hanging; you can still see yourself. The gold will sell for a good price.
Suggested line: You prise off the old gold frame and leave the mirror hanging, bare. It still shows whoever stands in front of it. It never needed the gold.
Why: The current line reads like a receipt; this keeps the gold and lands the room's point.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You find the brass collection plate bolted to the wall, marked for {villain_title}. You take the coins.
Suggested line: A little brass plate for donations to {villain_title}, bolted to the wall. It is quite full. You take the lot.
Why: Restores the flagged dry 'It is quite full' (token kept).

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You close your hand around the money and leave the empty plate.
Suggested line: It is, after all, other people's money. They would want it back.
Why: Restores the flagged wry justification; the current line just restates the action.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You find a pot of coins on the top landing, left as a tip by the last climber. You rub your legs and pocket it.
Suggested line: At the top, a pot of coins sits on the landing: a tip left by the last person who made it. You rub your legs and pocket the coins.
Why: Restores 'the last person who made it', which says what 500 identical steps cost.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You keep reading. Page after page describes work that helped people.
Suggested line: It goes on. They are good. They are so good.
Why: Restores the flagged motif; 'Page after page describes work that helped people' tells instead of shows.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You read the last plan twice. You recognise the care in it. You close the journal gently.
Suggested line: Once, he was exactly the person you would want running a kingdom. You close the last journal very gently.
Why: Restores the flagged line that makes Primm tragic before the Last Journal.

Speaker: The Wanderer
Effective line: I've walked a long way. Everyone I met was afraid of you.
Suggested line: Sorry. That's forest mud. I've walked a long way, and everyone I met on the way here was afraid of you.
Why: Restores the flagged first words to Primm: the Wanderer's own voice answering 'you have scuffed it'.

Speaker: Primm
Effective line: Every one of them has a number. I can account for every citizen. Nobody need be overlooked.
Suggested line: Every one of them has a number. Nobody is ever overlooked. Do you know how few kingdoms can say that?
Why: Restores Primm's flagged sincere, faintly proud question: numbering people as his gift.

Speaker: Primm
Effective line: Please remain still. I know how to put this right.
Suggested line: This will not hurt. It will, however, be Standard.
Why: Restores the flagged line: gracious, precise, and it names Phase 1 (Standardization).

Speaker: The Wanderer
Effective line: People are different. You know that.
Suggested line: Because some things are five. Some people are.
Why: Restores the direct answer to 'Why must anything be five?' (flagged callback).

Speaker: Primm, "His Perfection"
Effective line: People are different. You know that.
Suggested line: Because some things are five. Some people are.
Why: Same callback in the rushed variant.

Speaker: The Wanderer
Effective line: I'm not your subject. No order outranks treating people with respect.
Suggested line: And nobody files me under 'subject' again. No order outranks treating people with respect.
Why: Restores Agnes's closing-line callback (story bible section 21) and keeps the tested phrase.

Speaker: The Wanderer
Effective line: I'm not your subject. No order outranks treating people with respect.
Suggested line: Nobody files me under 'subject' again. No order outranks treating people with respect.
Why: Same Agnes callback in the Necrocrat-only variant, where she was certainly heard.

Speaker: Grandmaster Flex, the Unbroken
Effective line: You see Grandmaster Flex step from behind a pillar, unwinding a bandage from his arm. 'Breathe in. Hold.'
Suggested line: Grandmaster Flex steps out from behind a pillar, unwinding a very small bandage from a very large arm. 'Breathe in. Hold.'
Why: Restores the flagged image and drops 'You see'.

Speaker: The Grand Chef
Effective line: You see the Grand Chef in a clean apron, ladle in hand. 'Have you eaten? Let me help.'
Suggested line: The Grand Chef, in a clean apron, ladle in hand. 'Have you eaten? No. Of course you have not.'
Why: Restores her flagged voice: she answers her own question, as only she can.

Speaker: Agnes Overdue
Effective line: 'The rules must answer for him too.' (Agnes's Appeal: Necrocrat cards cost 1 less, and you gain 2 max HP.)
Suggested line: 'It applies to him, dear. It applies to him very well.' (Agnes's Appeal: Necrocrat cards cost 1 less, and you gain 2 max HP.)
Why: Restores the flagged Agnes line (her technicality, with relish); rule text unchanged.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You stand among the pieces of the model. Tiny houses lie scattered across the floor. The table no longer holds a kingdom.
Suggested line: The model lies in pieces. A hundred thousand tiny houses on the floor, all in the wrong places, and somehow they look better.
Why: Restores the flagged image: mess over perfection, the game's thesis in one sentence.

Speaker: Primm, "His Perfection"
Effective line: You took my mother and father. I can't even remember their faces. I'm letting go. I won't keep living in what you did.
Suggested line: You took my mother and father. I can't even remember their faces. I'm letting it go anyway. Watch.
Why: Restores the flagged answer: he shows Primm the letting-go instead of describing it (the earlier 'Watch how it's done' trimmed so it cannot read as a gloat).

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You hear the mirrors crack one by one. For the first time in ten years, {villain} sees himself in them.
Suggested line: The mirrors crack one by one, and for the first time in ten years {villain} sees himself in them.
Why: Drops the 'You hear' frame the earlier pass added; the image speaks for itself.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: Above the small kingdom, you see a tired man kneeling without his crown or his perfect smile.
Suggested line: No crown. No perfect smile. Only a tired man kneeling above a very small kingdom.
Why: Restores the flagged three-beat caption; the current one buries 'tired man' mid-sentence.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You stand in the light pouring through the broken glass.
Suggested line: Light pours in through the broken glass. It does not feel like winning. It feels like the end of a long, quiet lie.
Why: Restores the flagged 'end of a long, quiet lie' (the story bible quotes it), in present tense.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: The Necrocrat wing's archive is filing from floor to ceiling. On the desk, under a paperweight shaped like a peacock, lies a memo, the ink still wet.
Suggested line: The Necrocrat wing's archive is paper from floor to ceiling. On the desk, under a paperweight shaped like a peacock, lies a memo, the ink still wet.
Why: Fixes 'is filing from floor to ceiling' (reads as a typo).

Speaker: Nurse Hesper Dray
Effective line: 'Fell over. We rolled you in. Fee is yours. Drink the tea while it is hot; freedom hasn't changed that part.'
Suggested line: 'Fell over. We rolled you in. The fee is still yours. The tea is not free just because the kingdom is.'
Why: Restores the flagged Hesper sting; the current line explains itself.

Speaker: Old Fern
Effective line: Smell that? Honest compost. I could cry. Waste of water when I could be watering the patch. Come back any time.
Suggested line: Smell that? Honest compost. I could cry. Won't. Waste of good water. Come back any time.
Why: Same joke, half the words, in Fern's grumble.

Speaker: Widow Pell
Effective line: We visit every morning. I tell him about the people who helped us. I tell him about you.
Suggested line: We're well. My husband would have said you were late. He'd have meant it fondly.
Why: Restores the flagged Pell line; the current one repeats her intro ('every morning').

Speaker: Chef Marlo
Effective line: Flour on the ceiling. Food on the plates. Everything in its proper place, at last.
Suggested line: And chaotic. There is flour on the ceiling. I have never been so happy to have a mess.
Why: Restores the flagged line: 'everything in its proper place' is the regime's value, not liberation's.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Effective line: A hat of any size. I keep looking up, trying to decide.
Suggested line: I am going to wear a hat of any size. Maybe two at once.
Why: Restores the flagged freed joy (One Approved Hat Size pays off with two).

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Effective line: The bakery is painted on. We want a real one. None of us knows how to bake yet. Anyone can volunteer to be the first to burn a loaf.
Suggested line: The bakery is painted on. There is going to be a real one, as soon as someone learns to bake. I have a recipe. The recipe is: try.
Why: Restores the flagged punchline; the current line ends flat.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Effective line: The hedge is round. I kept trimming the corners, and then I wondered why I wanted corners.
Suggested line: The hedge is round. The hedge wanted to be round. I asked it. I did not have to submit a form.
Why: Restores the flagged payoff to the square-hedge setup; giddy and specific.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Effective line: Spontaneity every day! I don't know what comes next! I can hardly wait!
Suggested line: Spontaneity every day! I am exhausted! I am not sure I like it! I love it!
Why: Restores the flagged crooked joy; the current version is plain cheer.

Speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
Effective line: May I be honest? Your hat is awful. Thank you for wearing it.
Suggested line: I am not going to be polite today. I am going to be honest. Your hat is awful. I love it.
Why: Pays off her 'I am the politest person in the Showcase' setup (flagged).

Speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
Effective line: Attention, citizens. (a cough) This is a loudspeaker. Nobody is on the other end.
Suggested line: Attention, citizens. (a cough) The weather is no longer approved. It is just weather. It seems to be managing.
Why: Pays off the running gag (Plume approving the weather) on the same speaker slot that set it up.

Speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
Effective line: Attention, citizens! Any hat size is permitted. You may finally stop thinking about hat sizes.
Suggested line: Attention, citizens! Hats of any size are now permitted. Hats of negative size remain under review.
Why: Restores the flagged freed hat gag, still in broadcast voice.

Speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
Effective line: Attention, citizens! Spontaneity is no longer limited to Thursday. You may disregard this reminder.
Suggested line: Attention, citizens! Spontaneity Thursday is now every day. You may stop rehearsing your surprise.
Why: Undoes the 'rehearse your surprise' setup directly (the voice bible's freed-announcement rule).

Speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
Effective line: Attention, citizens. The Wrinkles were real. Please thank them.
Suggested line: Attention, citizens. The Wrinkles were real. Please thank anyone who exists.
Why: Turns 'Please report anyone who exists' into its payoff.

Speaker: Capital guards and clerks
Effective line: Nobody has told me where else to stand. I keep almost asking permission to go for a walk.
Suggested line: Nobody has told me where else to stand. I thought I might go for a walk. If that is... No. I am not asking. I am telling you. I think.
Why: Shows the running gag (almost asking permission) instead of stating it.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You hear the scale model split. The table cracks beneath it, and the sound travels through the castle walls.
Suggested line: The scale model cracks in half. Then the table cracks. Then, with the sound of a very large drawer being pulled from a very large cabinet, the castle walls begin to come down.
Why: Restores the precise, filing-cabinet image of Primm's castle falling; the current 'You hear' line is flat.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: In {showcase}, a painted door falls flat. You see a citizen step through onto the street beyond.
Suggested line: In {showcase}, a painted door falls flat, and a very surprised citizen steps through it onto a very real street.
Why: Restores painted door versus real street (the facade theme) and drops 'You see'.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You see Fig Sly among the people emerging from the Crease. He carries his stock with him.
Suggested line: Fig Sly comes up out of the Crease already selling something, to somebody, for some reason. Nobody stops him.
Why: Narration about him, not his line: restores the story bible beat ('already selling something') over a flat description.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You watch the four Paths gather around their leaders, carrying what they have saved from the past ten years.
Suggested line: The Beefcakes are late. The Necrocrats have brought a form. The Gourmands are overdressed. The Refusemancers smell, faintly, of compost.
Why: Restores the four Paths arriving in character (story bible beat 7); the current line is generic.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You see hands marked by iron, flour, ink and soil reach across the space between the four groups.
Suggested line: Muscle and stoves, records and soil: each was good alone. Together they ran a kingdom, argued about it every day, and it worked.
Why: Restores the game's thesis, which sets up 'The point was the argument' in the next box.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: You read the changes beneath it: MAY crossed out for SHOULD, then WILL, IF THEY FEEL LIKE IT. Four hands have left their marks.
Suggested line: Somebody has crossed out MAY and written SHOULD. Somebody else has crossed out SHOULD and written WILL, IF THEY FEEL LIKE IT. A pigeon sits on the full stop.
Why: Shows the four hands arguing on the wall instead of summarising it; the pigeon is the quiet last turn.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: For everyone who waited to be heard.
Suggested line: In memory of Form 27-B, Form 27-C and Form 27-B
Why: Credits may carry a joke: restores the forms callback over a generic dedication.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: For everyone learning to choose again.
Suggested line: No hats were harmed. Several were enlarged.
Why: Restores the regulation-hat callback; the credits had two near-identical dedications in a row.

Speaker: Agnes Overdue
Effective line: Thank you, dear. I have written it down, though that hardly seems enough.
Suggested line: I have filed a Form of Gratitude, dear. It was approved on the first attempt. Irregular.
Why: Pays off Agnes's 'Irregular.' gag and her denied appeals; the next box ('going to cry') stays sincere.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: the Pathwork Throne
Suggested line: The Pathwork Throne
Why: Title case, like every other beat title; the lower-case 'the' is a slip from the earlier pass.

Speaker: Agnes Overdue
Effective line: You see Maren make her way through the crowd. She stops in front of you, flour still on her sleeve.
Suggested line: Maren pushes through the crowd, tortoise-slow, and stops in front of you. There is flour on her sleeve.
Why: Keeps the flour, drops 'You see', and lets her slowness show how hard she is pushing.

Speaker: Primm, "His Perfection"
Effective line: He designs good drains. The guard stays here while he works.
Suggested line: He designs very good drains, it turns out. Do not tell him I said so.
Why: Current line has the guard call himself 'the guard'; this one also quietly withholds the praise Primm wants.

Speaker: Isla Brannoch
Effective line: You're the one who knocked the castle over? Dad says hi. Dad says a lot, actually. Thank you.
Suggested line: You're the one who knocked the castle over? Dad says thank you. That's what the 'Hm' meant. Thank you from me, too.
Why: 'Dad says a lot' contradicts the man who just said 'Hm.'; this reads his 'Hm' instead, warmly.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: In the Capital's square, you watch the leaders of the four Paths clasp hands. Several people cry.
Suggested line: In the Capital's square, the leaders of the four Paths clasp hands. Nobody trips. Several people cry.
Why: Drops 'you watch' and restores 'Nobody trips.', the small turn that keeps the still from being solemn.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: Above you, four banners share one crowded pole.
Suggested line: Four banners fly from the same pole. It is a little crowded, and nobody minds.
Why: Restores 'and nobody minds', which says the whole ending in five words.

Speaker: (narration)
Effective line: At the crowd's edge, you see a hooded traveler smile, leaves still in their hair. There is always another path.
Suggested line: At the edge of the crowd, a hooded traveler smiles, leaves still in their hair. There is always another path.
Why: Drops 'you see'; the traveler is the player, so narrating that 'you see' him reads oddly.

Speaker: The Rescuer (Elowen)
Effective line: Get up, Dad. You're going to Crosspath. Agnes has a form for you, Maren has a great deal to say, and you are going to listen to all of it.
Suggested line: Get up, Dad. You're going to {town}. Agnes has a form for you, Maren has a great deal to say, and you are going to listen to all of it.
Why: Story files use the token, not the literal town name (canon rule; renders the same).

Speaker: The Rescuer (Elowen)
Effective line: No. It was yours too. Get up. You're going to Crosspath, and you're going to listen to every word Maren says.
Suggested line: No. It was yours too. Get up. You're going to {town}, and you're going to listen to every word Maren says.
Why: Story files use the token, not the literal town name (canon rule; renders the same).
